s1.syndrome_frame: Acute skin and soft tissue infection with ulceration and nodules at a previous intravenous catheter site, complicated by recent hospitalization and bacterial pneumonia
salient_findings: Painful ulceration on the right distal forearm
Tender red nodules in the right antecubital fossa
Marked superficial and deep inflammation with tissue necrosis and gram-positive bacilli on histopathologic examination
key_facts: Recent hospitalization for congestive heart failure
Development of ulceration at a previous peripheral intravenous catheter site
Recent activities included cleaning a fish tank, playing with a pet cat, and gardening
No recent travel history or immunosuppressive medications
Readmission for bacterial pneumonia
Ulcerated plaque on the right forearm with tender red nodules
Histopathologic examination showed marked inflammation and tissue necrosis
Gram stain identified multiple filamentous gram-positive bacilli
Tissue culture was positive for a specific organism

shortlist.label: Nocardia infection
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain identified multiple filamentous gram-positive bacilli, consistent with Nocardia

shortlist.label: Actinomadura infection
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Nocardia, Actinomadura is a gram-positive bacillus that can cause skin and soft tissue infections

shortlist.label: Streptomyces infection
shortlist.why_kept: Streptomyces is another gram-positive bacillus that can cause skin and soft tissue infections, although less common than Nocardia

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium marinum infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's recent activity of cleaning a fish tank is a risk factor for Mycobacterium marinum infection

shortlist.label: Mycobacterium ulcerans infection
shortlist.why_kept: Although less common, Mycobacterium ulcerans can cause skin and soft tissue infections, and the patient's gardening activity may be a risk factor
